messages:
sana: Quick heads-up - onboarding sample app sent duplicate webhooks when a 429 happened during token rotation. Repro attached.
jordan: Node sample or Go?
sana: Node. Timeline: initial request -> 429, token refresh in flight -> client retries with refreshed token -> server processed both. Sample sets `Idempotency-Key` but retry path dropped it.
mike: That aligns with earlier whitelist clone bug. We rebuild requests on refresh and can lose headers.
olga: Parity issue across SDKs too (Go uses `x-rw-idempotency`, Python uses `Idempotency-Key`). We should pick a canonical header and normalize. Proposal: `x-redwood-idempotency` (lowercase).
kevin: Short-term mitigation: 1) ensure token refresh preserves idempotency header in Node SDK; 2) add optional client-side retry guard (in-process TTL map keyed by idempotency token, default 3s) behind feature flag `client_retry_guard`.
sana: I'll open PR for Node fix + prototype retry guard with unit tests and an e2e script that simulates token rotate + 429. Will include README note about setting idempotency keys and avoiding auto-replays for payment endpoints.
jordan: add telemetry when a retry is suppressed so we can measure. devex-bot: file an incident if suppression rate > 0.5% over 5m.
mike: Reminder: guard is a stopgap. Server-side dedupe required for multi-instance customers. Long-term: accept canonical header server-side and return `Idempotency-Cache: cached|new`.
olga: I'll draft a small RFC for header canonicalization + response header and update SDK migration guide.
kevin: Also add sampleapp CI test that rotates tokens mid-request and asserts no duplicate side effects.
sana: will ping reviewers @mike @olga. Opening PR in a few hours. :thumbsup:
